description: Queue an AI task or recurring job to run at the cleanest grid hour before its deadline; long deadlines may use the provider Batch API. Use when: the user defers work ("tonight", "no rush", "before my limit resets") or wants it repeated ("every night", "daily", a cron); map that to deadline or repeat. Do not use for work the user waits on (do it now), to preview only (use recommend_window or dry_run) or for limits (use tidegap_usage). Behavior: adds one task, one run of one runner (dry_run writes nothing), or with repeat a job of such tasks; `tidegap tick` runs it; reads the grid forecast; no login; the result stays in the queue (check_queue_status). Returns: task_id, status, scheduled_for, deadline, provider, model, runs_in, estimated_carbon_g_co2, a readiness line; a job adds job_id and its guarantee. Rejects a past deadline, an unknown zone, disallowed tools and shell commands.

after_limit_reset.description: true when the user says "after my limit resets": the task starts no earlier than the Claude subscription limit reset (the latest reset of an exhausted 5-hour or weekly window, else the fuller window's reset; see tidegap_usage), then runs at the cleanest hour after it. The deadline rises to at least two hours after the reset. Fails, queuing nothing, when no limit reading exists. Defaults to false; cannot combine with not_before.

candidates.description: 'provider:model' pairs the user allows, e.g. ['anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5','ollama:llama-3-1-8b']. With 2 or more, the scheduler scores each at the chosen window on carbon, cost and latency (see route_weights), runs the winner and records the scores on the receipt; it never picks a model outside this list. Omit, or pass one entry, to keep provider and model as given. A model missing from the price table is rejected.

carbon_budget_g.description: Hard cap on the task's estimated grams CO2e, e.g. 5. Windows above it are skipped; if no window before the deadline fits, the task fails instead of running on a dirty grid. Omit for no cap.

cwd.description: Absolute folder a 'claude-code' run works in, e.g. a worktree '/work/app/.worktrees/fix-login'. This session's project folder keeps the run in a copy of this session; another folder runs fresh there, told where the task came from. Rejected: '/', the home folder, a folder another user owns, home dot folders, ~/Library and .git folders. Omit to run in the session's project folder, or a temporary folder without a session.

days.description: Weekdays for repeat 'weekly', e.g. ['mon','thu'] for "Mondays and Thursdays". Defaults to today's weekday in time_zone; omit for any other repeat.

deadline.description: When the task must be finished: ISO-8601 with a UTC offset, in the future. Convert the user's words, e.g. "by 8am tomorrow" in New York becomes '2026-05-13T08:00:00-04:00'. Omit with deadline_kind 'quota_reset', which sets it (a value is then ignored), or with a job repeat, whose first run then follows the cadence.

deadline_kind.description: Defaults to 'absolute': the deadline parameter sets the due time. 'quota_reset' sets it to the next weekly subscription-quota reset minus a margin, from ~/.tidegap/config (TIDEGAP_QUOTA_RESET_<LABEL>=<weekday> <HH:MM> [<IANA zone>]; margin TIDEGAP_QUOTA_MARGIN_H_<LABEL>, default 2 hours). Use it when the user says "before my weekly limit resets". A due time more than 24 hours away can use the provider Batch API.

dispatch.description: Defaults to true: store a task that `tidegap tick` runs. false queues an in-memory placeholder that never calls a model (tests only) and cannot combine with not_before or after_limit_reset. Omit it in normal use.

dry_run.description: true previews the plan (window, carbon estimate, provider, model, runs_in) and queues nothing, e.g. to confirm with the user first. Defaults to false.

every_hours.description: Hours between runs for repeat 'every_n_hours', e.g. 6 for "every 6 hours". Each run comes at most this long after the previous start and not sooner than half of it. Required with 'every_n_hours'; omit for any other repeat.

model.description: Model id for the chosen provider, e.g. 'claude-sonnet-5' (anthropic) or 'gpt-6-sol' (openai). Omit for the provider default: anthropic 'claude-sonnet-5' (TIDEGAP_DEFAULT_MODEL overrides it), openai 'gpt-6-sol', gemini 'gemini-3.8-flash', ollama 'llama3.1'. With 2 or more candidates, routing may pick another model from that list.

not_before.description: Earliest start, ISO-8601 with offset, e.g. '2026-05-12T18:00:00+02:00' for "not before 6pm" or "after lunch". The task then runs at the cleanest hour between it and the deadline; it must be in the future and not after the deadline. It is a bound, not a run time: with not_before 70 minutes away and a 3-hour deadline, the task can run near the end. Omit to allow any time up to the deadline; cannot combine with after_limit_reset.

origin_session_id.description: Claude Code session id of the conversation that queued the task. Omit it: the server finds the current session itself when the Tidegap plugin is installed. Pass it only when the host substitutes it (e.g. ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID} in a slash command); it then wins. Values that are not 8-128 letters, digits, '-' or '_' are ignored.

output_path.description: Absolute file path inside cwd, this session's project folder or the temp folder, e.g. '/tmp/digest.json'; when the task completes, { taskId, result, receipt } is written there as JSON, replacing a regular file you own. Its folder must exist; a name starting with '.', ~/.ssh, ~/.config, ~/Library and similar folders are rejected. Omit to keep the result only in the queue (check_queue_status).

permission_profile.description: Tool set of a 'claude-code' run: 'read' is Read, Grep and Glob in its folder; 'web' is WebSearch and WebFetch in a fresh temporary folder (no cwd); 'none' is no tools. Runs never get Bash, Write or Edit. Defaults to 'read' when cwd is given; omit both for tools or its default. Rejected when tools names another set.

prompt.description: The full instruction the model receives when the window arrives, e.g. 'Summarize today's AI policy news in 5 bullets'. The run may start in a fresh session without this conversation (the reply's runs_in line says which), so name the files, decisions and constraints it needs.

provider.description: Where the task runs. 'claude-code' uses the local Claude Code login on the next `tidegap tick`, with no API key (see tools); 'ollama' is a local model; the others need their API key. Defaults to 'claude-code' when queued from a Claude Code session (it then runs in a copy of that session, in its project directory), else 'anthropic'; an explicit 'anthropic' never resumes a session. 'anthropic' and 'openai' can use the 50%-cheaper Batch API when the deadline allows; the others always run synchronously.

quota_provider.description: Which configured quota to follow with deadline_kind 'quota_reset', e.g. 'claude' or 'codex'. Omit when exactly one label is configured; rejected with any other deadline_kind.

redact_in_receipt.description: Regex patterns removed from the prompt before it is stored on the receipt, e.g. ['customer-[0-9]+'] for customer ids. Omit for the default, which strips API-key-looking strings.

region.description: Grid zone to plan against, e.g. 'US-CAL-CISO' or 'FR'; pass it only when the user names a place. `tidegap region list` prints the supported zones; any zone works with an Electricity Maps key. Defaults to the host's configured region (MCP: TIDEGAP_DEFAULT_REGION; OpenClaw: defaultRegion), else the stored setting (`tidegap region set`), else a time-zone guess, else GB. The reply's region_source names the rule that applied.

repeat.description: Defaults to 'none', a one-off. 'daily', 'weekdays', 'weekly' and 'every_n_hours' create a job: each run is a new task with this prompt, started fresh (never a copy of this session) in this project at the cleanest hour of its period, e.g. "every night" is 'daily' with window '22:00-08:00'. A job rejects per-task options (region, carbon_budget_g, candidates, not_before, dry_run and the like). With deadline_kind 'quota_reset', 'daily', 'weekly' and 'quota_reset' start the older series instead, which follows the quota reset; 'weekdays' and 'every_n_hours' are rejected there. End a job or series with cancel_task series=true.

result_path.description: Absolute path of a new file, e.g. '/tmp/review.md'. When the task completes, Tidegap (never the run) writes the result text there with mode 0600, and the session's notice names it. It must be inside cwd, this session's project folder or the temp folder; rejected: an existing file, a name starting with '.', ~/.ssh, ~/.config, ~/Library and similar folders. Omit to keep the result in the queue only (check_queue_status).

route_weights.description: How to rank candidates, e.g. {"carbon": 1} for carbon only. Weights are relative and normalized; a key left out counts as 0. Omit for the default {carbon: 0.6, cost: 0.3, latency: 0.1}. Ignored unless candidates has 2 or more entries.

carbon.description: Relative weight on the estimated grams CO2e at the chosen window. Omit to weight it 0 when route_weights is given.

cost.description: Relative weight on the estimated USD list cost, batch discount included when eligible. Omit to weight it 0 when route_weights is given.

latency.description: Relative weight on speed: local beats hosted sync, which beats hosted batch. Omit to weight it 0 when route_weights is given.

runner.description: Another name for provider, e.g. 'claude-code'; pass one of the two, or both with the same value. Omit it to follow provider and its default. 'command' is rejected: a shell command task is the user's call, queued with `tidegap queue add --runner command`.

time_zone.description: IANA zone that window and days are read in, e.g. 'Europe/Berlin'; take it from the user's location. Defaults to the host's system zone. Only with a job repeat.

title.description: Short label for queue lists, e.g. 'Weekly digest'. Defaults to the prompt's first line, cut to 80 characters; API-key-looking strings are redacted.

tools.description: Claude Code tools for a 'claude-code' run, e.g. ['WebSearch','WebFetch'] for a research task; [] means none. Allowed: WebSearch, WebFetch, Read, Grep, Glob. Omit for the default: Read, Grep and Glob in the session's project directory for a task queued from a Claude Code session, else WebSearch and WebFetch (TIDEGAP_CLAUDE_TOOLS overrides that one). A web tool makes a task from a session run fresh, without its context. Rejected: any other name (Bash, Write, Edit, ...) and a set that mixes a file tool with a web tool, because web content is untrusted. A job keeps the whole group: any file tool means Read, Grep and Glob; any web tool means WebSearch and WebFetch. A job stores its tools when created and ignores TIDEGAP_CLAUDE_TOOLS.

wake_session.description: true wakes this Claude Code session when the task finishes, if it sits idle, within 12 hours after its last turn ended: the session starts a turn by itself with the notice. A wake spends a model turn while nobody may be watching, so set it only when the user wants the result acted on at once. Rejected outside a Claude Code session. Omit (default false) to get the notice with the next prompt.

window.description: Local hours a job may run in, 'HH:MM-HH:MM', e.g. '22:00-08:00' for "at night"; '22:00-06:00' crosses midnight. Each run then picks its cleanest hour inside that day's window. Only with repeat 'daily', 'weekdays' or 'weekly'; omit to allow any hour.

name: schedule_task
